title: TTP

description.main: A five-year series of deadpan photographs of a single ping pong table in a Leipzig park, taken from the photographer's window. Winner of the 2018 MACK First Book Award.
description.extended:
TTP is the first book by the photographer Hayahisa Tomiyasu. It follows one ping pong table in a Leipzig park over five years, always from the same window.

Tomiyasu shot the table from the eighth-floor window of his former student apartment, facing south. The framing barely moves. What changes is the light, the season and who turns up. The title abbreviates tischtennisplatte, the German word for a table tennis table. The table serves as a sun bed, a laundry counter, a skate obstacle, a climbing frame, a lunch spot and a refuge from the street. It is put to nearly every use except table tennis. The pictures are deadpan and patient, and the book becomes a record of the habits of the people who pass through.

MACK published it in 2018 as the winner of the MACK First Book Award, a 260-page paperback measuring 20 x 27 cm. It was also shortlisted for the 44th Ihei Kimura Prize.
description.artist_bio: Hayahisa Tomiyasu is a Japanese photographer who made TTP while a student in Leipzig; it is his first book.

notes: MACK's only live product page found is the 'first edition, fourth printing' (June 2021) listing; the ISBN is the same for all printings (Twelvebooks confirms 2018, 9781912339242). Library copy's printing is unknown. No official artist site found (hayahisatomiyasu.com and similar do not resolve), so authors[0].url is null. No source states the photographer's pronouns; the description uses 'his' only in 'his former student apartment', which is MACK's own wording, so change to 'the' if you want it neutral. Cover is a crop of MACK's 3/4-angle product shot (2717x2598 source, front face cropped to 1490x2150); slight perspective skew and a faint shadow along the bottom edge. Awards: MACK First Book Award 2018 (MACK page), shortlist for the 44th Ihei Kimura Prize (Twelvebooks page).
